hints: Set $y = 0$ in either curve equation to find the coordinates of $A$ on the $x$-axis.
walkthrough:
Set $y = 0$ in either curve equation to find the $x$-intercept $A$:
$$(1 - 2x)^{1/2} = 0 \implies 1 - 2x = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{2}$$

hints: Integrate $\int_0^{1/2} (1-2x)^{1/2}\,dx$ using the reverse chain rule.
Subtract the lower curve integral from the upper curve integral.
walkthrough:
Set up the integral for the area between the two curves from $x = 0$ to $x = \frac{1}{2}$:
$$\text{Area} = \int_0^{1/2} (1 - 2x)^{1/2}\,dx - \int_0^{1/2} (2x - 1)^2\,dx$$

Integrate the upper curve $(1 - 2x)^{1/2}$ with respect to $x$:
$$\int_0^{1/2} (1 - 2x)^{1/2}\,dx = \left[ -\frac{1}{3}(1 - 2x)^{3/2} \right]_0^{1/2} = 0 - \left(-\frac{1}{3}(1)^{3/2}\right) = \frac{1}{3}$$

Integrate the lower curve $(2x - 1)^2$ with respect to $x$:
$$\int_0^{1/2} (2x - 1)^2\,dx = \left[ \frac{(2x - 1)^3}{6} \right]_0^{1/2} = 0 - \left(\frac{(-1)^3}{6}\right) = \frac{1}{6}$$

Subtract the two values to obtain the shaded area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{6}$$
